title: Focus Funnel — 21-day personal KPI sprint (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight, iterating scratchpad for a 21-day focus sprint. Goal: move from vague intentions ("do more deep work") to clear lead indicators that reliably increase my product output and reduce context-switching overhead.

Why now:
- Q1 felt noisy: many half-started experiments and 3-4 context switches per day.
- Team velocity is improving; I want to match that by stabilizing my personal throughput.

North-star outcome (end of 21d):
- 3 shipped experiments (small essays, a monitoring script, one internal doc + PR)
- median deep-focus block = 90 minutes (was ~45)
- streak index (days with at least one quality block) >= 18/21

Hypotheses (H):
H1: If I reserve two morning focus blocks (8:30–10:00, 10:30–11:30) and treat them as meeting-free, I will double uninterrupted work time and increase shipped experiments.
H2: If I pre-define micro-deliverables for each block (15–30m), I reduce procrastination and context switching.
H3: If I log a 3-line end-of-day note (what shipped, blocker, next micro-step) I reduce re-onboarding cost and unblock next day faster.

Lead indicators (what I'll measure daily):
- Focus blocks completed (int): target 2/day
- Focus minutes total (int): target >= 120/day
- Micro-deliverables completed (int): target >= 2/day
- End-of-day journal (yes/no): target yes
- Interruptions during blocks (int): minimize to 0–1

Lag indicators (outcomes):
- Experiments shipped (cumulative): target 3 by day 21
- Median focus block (minutes): target 90
- Streak index: target >= 18

Operational rules (scratch, flexible):
- Mornings are sacred: no meetings during first two blocks unless emergency.
- Calendar blocks: 8:20–10:00, quick 20m slack, 10:20–11:30. Blocks must have a clear micro-deliverable pinned in title.
- Use a single TODO list (one list only) for micro-deliverables; mark as done inside block.
- If interrupted: 1) log reason in the note, 2) try to reclaim 25% of remaining block time resuming within 60m.

Weekly check cadence: quick self-review on Sun evenings (15m) + 10m retro each Friday

Measurement plan (manual, minimalist):
- Use a Focus Simple spreadsheet (local) to record blocks and minutes.
- End-of-day note pasted into this doc under a date header.
- Weekly summary computed manually on days 7, 14, 21.

Template for end-of-day note (copy/paste):
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Blocks: 2 (8:30–10:00 done, 10:30–11:10 truncated)
- Minutes: 130
- Micro-deliverables: 3 (write internal doc outline; fix monitoring script; PR draft)
- Interruptions: Slack (1), meeting (0)
- Blockers: waiting on ccs for PR review
- Quick wins: outline landed, PR ready to request review
- Next micro-step: push PR and add unit test (20m)

Progress notes (live):
2026-02-20 (Day 1)
- Blocks: 2, Minutes: 125, Micro: 2, Journal: yes
- Observations: Strong morning energy but opened Slack mid-block twice. Need to mute mobile notifications.

2026-02-23 (Day 4)
- Blocks: 1 (had unexpected all-hands), Minutes: 60, Micro: 1, Journal: yes
- Observations: All-hands killed second block; consider moving second block earlier to 10:00–11:00 on all-hands days.

2026-02-28 (End of Week 1)
- Cumulative shipped: 0 (still writing outlines), median block: 70m, streak: 6/7
- Quick retro: sticky slack interruptions -> enforce mobile mute + short auto-reply during blocks. Micro-deliverables are helping.

2026-03-07 (End of Week 2)
- Cumulative shipped: 1 (internal doc + PR), median block: 85m, streak: 13/14
- Retro notes: Moving second block earlier on meeting-heavy days helped. Need to batch PR review nudge on Tuesdays.

Quick list of tactics to try (fast experiments):
- Auto-responder during blocks: short message + triage time at 11:30.
- Keyboard shortcut macros for three common git commands to reduce friction.
- 20-minute planning micro-step pinned to each block to reduce context switch time.
- Batch quick async responses into one 30m window post-lunch.

Risks and decision points:
- Risk: Over-optimizing calendar could make me inflexible for truly urgent issues. Decision: keep one flexible slot per day for urgent cross-team signals.
- Risk: Focus blocks become low-value busywork. Decision: micro-deliverables must be outcome-focused, not just "do something".

Open questions (to resolve during sprint):
- What is the ideal length for the second block on meeting-heavy days? 45m or 60m?
- Which two days per week should I prioritize longer blocks for deep experiments? Candidate: Tue/Thu.

Personal note to self:
- If momentum drops for 3 consecutive days, pause the sprint and diagnose instead of doubling down. Reward small wins (coffee + 30m reading) when early signals are positive.

Archive plan:
- At end of 21 days copy this doc -> \shared_notes/personal-sprints/ and create a short public note with what worked + playbook for repeated use.

Links/references:
- Quick inspiration: "Atomic Habits" chapter notes (local)
- Related team habit playbook: CONFLUENCE-TEAM/habits-brief

Next actions (today):
- Mute mobile notifications for morning blocks (done)
- Add micro-deliverable titles to both morning blocks (10m)
- Create quick git macro for PR create (15m)

--
Notes: keep this as the living scratchpad. If collaborators are useful, invite one accountability partner for weekly 10m sync.
